In the aligned Gaussian case, we derive the zeta-function poles for direct imaging and SPADE, show that both share the same real log canonical threshold $λ=1/2$ but differ in multiplicity, and obtain the corresponding Bayes free-energy asymptotics. This yields a universal subleading advantage of aligned SPADE in the local prior-weighted regime. In the misaligned setting, we study a physically motivated binary-SPADE reduction that retains the full leading $O(s^2)$ leakage contrast near alignment, with corrections from the detailed higher-mode redistribution entering only at $O(s^4)$. We show that misaligned binary-SPADE and direct imaging acquire nontrivial local power on different intrinsic scales, $s=O(n^{-1/4})$ and $s=O(n^{-1/2})$, respectively. However, finite-$n$ Neyman--Pearson comparisons under common physical conditions reveal that direct imaging is stronger on the plotted grids and that misaligned binary-SPADE exhibits an exact blind separation $s^\ast=2θ$, where its power collapses to $α$. These results identify model singularity as a structural organizing principle for finite-photon quantum discrimination and clarify how ideal aligned SPADE benchmarks can fail to translate into finite-$n$ advantages under misalignment.

AI.tldr: This paper uses singular learning theory to analyze far-field discrimination between one and two incoherent point sources, comparing direct imaging and SPADE under both aligned and misaligned conditions. It derives zeta-function poles, shows both methods share the same real log canonical threshold λ=1/2 but differ in multiplicity, revealing a universal subleading advantage of aligned SPADE. Under misalignment, binary-SPADE and direct imaging operate on different intrinsic scales (n^{-1/4} vs n^{-1/2}), and finite-n Neyman-Pearson tests show direct imaging outperforms on practical grids while misaligned binary-SPADE exhibits an exact blind separation where its power collapses to α.
AI.motivation: To understand the finite-photon behavior near the one-source boundary and the effect of realistic misalignment imperfections on quantum-optimal SPADE discrimination, which were previously less understood.
AI.method: Singular learning theory analysis of aligned Gaussian case (deriving zeta-function poles, real log canonical thresholds, Bayes free-energy asymptotics) and a binary-SPADE reduction for the misaligned setting, with finite-n Neyman-Pearson comparisons.
AI.result: Aligned SPADE and direct imaging share λ=1/2 but differ in multiplicity; misaligned binary-SPADE and direct imaging operate on scales n^{-1/4} and n^{-1/2} respectively; finite-n comparisons show direct imaging stronger on plotted grids; misaligned binary-SPADE has exact blind separation at s*=2θ.
AI.conclusion: Model singularity serves as a structural organizing principle for finite-photon quantum discrimination, and ideal aligned SPADE advantages may not translate to finite-n advantages under misalignment.

title: Discrete-phase-randomized mode-pairing quantum key distribution
summary: Mode-pairing quantum key distribution (MP-QKD) protocol achieves performance beyond the repeaterless rate-transmittance bound and exhibits excellent practicality by avoiding the requirement for difficult global phase locking. However, the source side of MP-QKD still relies on the assumption of continuous phase randomization, an experimentally infeasible requirement in practice. Therefore, the practical security of the protocol cannot be fully guaranteed. In this work, we propose a discrete-phase-randomized mode-pairing quantum key distribution (DPR-MP-QKD) protocol and analyze the basis-dependence of the source side. Then, we introduce a concrete discrete version of the decoy state method that ensures the security of the DPR-MP-QKD protocol. Finally, simulation results indicate that as the number of discrete phases increases, the key rate performance of DPR-MP-QKD progressively approaches that of the continuous case, with convergence achieved at approximately 14 discrete phases. Moreover, our approach drastically lowers the demand for randomness. While conventional continuous phase randomization demands an unlimited supply of random bits, we show that merely a few bits (e.g., 4) are adequate.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a discrete-phase-randomized mode-pairing QKD (DPR-MP-QKD) protocol that replaces the impractical continuous phase randomization with discrete phase randomization. Security is analyzed via basis-dependence and a discrete decoy state method. With ~14 discrete phases, performance approaches the continuous case, and only a few random bits (e.g., 4) are needed.
AI.motivation: MP-QKD requires continuous phase randomization on the source side, which is experimentally infeasible, so practical security cannot be fully guaranteed.
AI.method: Proposes DPR-MP-QKD with discrete phase randomization, analyzes source-side basis-dependence, and introduces a discrete version of the decoy state method for security.
AI.result: With ~14 discrete phases, key rate approaches the continuous case. Only a few random bits (e.g., 4) are sufficient, drastically lowering randomness requirements.
AI.conclusion: DPR-MP-QKD enhances practical security by replacing continuous phase randomization with a discrete version, achieving near-continuous performance with far fewer random bits.

title: Spin chirality across quantum state copies detects hidden entanglement
comment: Main text: 16 pages, 3 figures. Supplementary Information: 46 pages, 12 figures, 18 tables
summary: Entanglement can hide in two fundamentally different ways. First, multi-copy correlations can carry information that no single-copy measurement on an unknown state is able to access. Second, bound entangled states possess a positive partial transpose, which makes them invisible to the Peres-Horodecki criterion and all moment inequalities that depend on it. Here we show that the moment difference between the partial transpose and purity decomposes exactly as a chirality-chirality correlator, where the relevant operator is the scalar spin chirality -- the same quantity that governs chiral spin liquids and the topological Hall effect. This decomposition identifies the specific physical structure that multi-copy entanglement detection probes. Using the same controlled-SWAP circuits, we develop a multi-channel spectral classifier for bound entanglement. The classifier combines realignment spectral features with chirality corrections and achieves 99.9% recall at zero false positives across all three known 3x3 bound entangled families, compared with ~40% for the CCNR criterion alone. We also introduce a marginal-noise construction that produces CCNR-invisible bound entangled states, which the classifier detects but which remain invisible to all single-parameter criteria. We validate our approach experimentally on three IBM Quantum processors and demonstrate negativity reconstruction with mean errors of 0.002-0.027, chirality detection for pure and mixed entangled states, and bound entanglement detection across two structurally distinct families (Horodecki and chessboard) on a single gate-based superconducting processor.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the moment difference between partial transpose and purity decomposes exactly as a scalar spin chirality-chirality correlator, linking multi-copy entanglement detection to chiral spin liquids and the topological Hall effect. Using controlled-SWAP circuits, the authors develop a multi-channel spectral classifier for bound entanglement that achieves 99.9% recall at zero false positives across all known 3×3 bound entangled families, and validate it experimentally on IBM Quantum processors.
AI.motivation: To understand the two fundamental ways entanglement can hide (multi-copy correlations and bound entanglement with positive partial transpose), and to develop a unified detection framework that reveals the physical structure behind multi-copy entanglement detection.
AI.method: The authors decompose the moment difference between partial transpose and purity as a chirality-chirality correlator, where the relevant operator is scalar spin chirality. They build a multi-channel spectral classifier using controlled-SWAP circuits, combining realignment spectral features with chirality corrections.
AI.result: 99.9% recall at zero false positives across all three known 3×3 bound entangled families (vs. ~40% for CCNR). Negativity reconstruction with mean errors of 0.002-0.027. Successful chirality detection and bound entanglement detection on IBM Quantum processors.
AI.conclusion: Multi-copy entanglement detection probes scalar spin chirality structure. The multi-channel classifier significantly outperforms single-parameter criteria and can detect a newly introduced class of CCNR-invisible bound entangled states. The approach is experimentally validated on noisy quantum hardware.

title: HQTN-SER: Speech Emotion Recognition with Hybrid Quantum Tensor Networks
summary: Speech emotion recognition (SER) remains fragile in real-world conditions because emotional cues are subtle, speaker-dependent, and easily confounded by recording variability, while high-performing deep models typically rely on large and carefully curated training sets. Quantum machine learning offers an alternative way to introduce nonlinear correlation modeling with compact modules, yet existing quantum SER studies remain limited and the impact of circuit structure is not well understood. This paper presents HQTN-SER, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that investigates how quantum tensor network connectivity can support SER under small-qubit settings. HQTN-SER introduces (i) an MPS-inspired quantum tensor network module that enforces structured interactions to model correlations in speech representations with a small number of trainable parameters, and (ii) a fusion strategy that combines quantum measurement features with a learned classical latent embedding for end-to-end emotion classification. We evaluate HQTN-SER on three public benchmarks (RAVDESS, SAVEE, and MDER) under a unified preprocessing and training protocol. The proposed model achieves consistent performance across datasets, RAVDESS = 80.12%, SAVEE = 78.26% and MDER = 73.51% accuracy, with stable convergence and low qubit counts, showing that tensor network structure can be an effective and hardware-aware design choice for quantum-assisted SER. The results provide a reproducible baseline and clarify when structured quantum modules can add value to affective computing today.

AI.tldr: HQTN-SER is a hybrid quantum-classical framework for speech emotion recognition that uses MPS-inspired quantum tensor network modules to model correlations with few parameters and low qubit counts, achieving 80.12%, 78.26%, and 73.51% accuracy on RAVDESS, SAVEE, and MDER respectively.
AI.motivation: SER is fragile in real-world conditions due to subtle, speaker-dependent, and confounded emotional cues; high-performing deep models require large curated datasets, and existing quantum SER studies are limited with poorly understood circuit structure impact.
AI.method: HQTN-SER introduces (i) an MPS-inspired quantum tensor network module enforcing structured interactions to model speech representation correlations with few trainable parameters, and (ii) a fusion strategy combining quantum measurement features with a learned classical latent embedding for end-to-end emotion classification.
AI.result: Achieves 80.12% on RAVDESS, 78.26% on SAVEE, and 73.51% on MDER with stable convergence and low qubit counts.
AI.conclusion: Tensor network structure is an effective and hardware-aware design choice for quantum-assisted SER, providing a reproducible baseline and clarifying when structured quantum modules can add value to affective computing.

title: Quantum-enabled complete RF-polarimetry with an optically-wired atomic sensor
summary: Rydberg atomic electrometry leverages the extreme sensitivity of highly excited atoms for calibration-free electric field measurements. The technique uses a non-metallic vapor cell to link properties of an RF field to a spectroscopic readout in the optical domain. Most demonstrations have so far focused on detecting linearly-polarized fields, for which the induced splitting of dressed atomic levels is rotationally invariant. Here we report on Rydberg atomic measurements of RF fields in a general state of polarization (SOP) which we map onto the Poincaré sphere through spectroscopic fingerprints. For a Stokes vector circumnavigating a Poincaré sphere meridian, we witness a continuous transformation of the atomic eigenenergy spectrum. Because the relative positions of eigenenergies are locked in place by quantization of angular momentum, the framework is universal and calibration free. We provide a specific demonstration in rubidium, which generalizes to all systems with a single valence electron.

AI.tldr: The paper extends Rydberg atomic electrometry to measure RF fields in arbitrary polarization states by mapping spectroscopic fingerprints onto the Poincaré sphere, demonstrating a universal, calibration-free framework for general polarization measurement.
AI.motivation: Previous Rydberg electrometry focused on linearly-polarized fields, where the induced splitting is rotationally invariant. The researchers sought to extend the technique to arbitrary polarization states, which is necessary for fully characterizing RF fields.
AI.method: The authors map the state of polarization (SOP) of an RF field onto the Poincaré sphere using spectroscopic fingerprints. They observe the continuous transformation of the atomic eigenenergy spectrum as a Stokes vector circumnavigates a Poincaré sphere meridian, leveraging angular momentum quantization for a calibration-free framework.
AI.result: The continuous transformation of the atomic eigenenergy spectrum was witnessed as the polarization state varied. The framework was demonstrated in rubidium and is generalizable to all systems with a single valence electron.
AI.conclusion: The framework is universal and calibration-free because the relative positions of eigenenergies are locked by angular momentum quantization. This generalizes Rydberg electrometry to arbitrary RF polarization states, extending beyond previous linear-polarization-only demonstrations.

title: Are free choices absolute, when internalized in Wigner's friend?
summary: Wigner's thought experiment illustrates quantum theory's measurement problem by considering an observer who measures a quantum system inside a sealed lab, modeled unitarily by an outsider. Recent extensions of this thought experiment, referred to as extended Wigner's friend arguments, question how different observers can reason consistently about each other in quantum setups, and challenge the absoluteness of the outcome value obtained by the friend under a notion of locality. In this work, we present an argument against the absoluteness of free choices under the same notion of locality, using an extended Wigner's friend scenario based on the Pusey--Barrett--Rudolph theorem. Similar arguments based on other contextuality or nonlocality models are possible.

AI.tldr: This paper argues against the absoluteness of free choices under a locality-based notion using an extended Wigner's friend scenario based on the PBR theorem, extending the critique from outcome absoluteness to free choice absoluteness.
AI.motivation: To challenge the absoluteness of free choices in quantum theory, extending the critique of outcome absoluteness from extended Wigner's friend arguments to free choices, using a similar locality-based notion.
AI.method: The paper presents an argument against the absoluteness of free choices using an extended Wigner's friend scenario built on the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph (PBR) theorem, with possible extensions using other contextuality or nonlocality models.
AI.result: Under the notion of locality used in extended Wigner's friend arguments, free choices cannot be considered absolute, analogous to how outcome values lose absoluteness.
AI.conclusion: The absoluteness of free choices is undermined by quantum reasoning in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, paralleling existing arguments about outcome absoluteness, with multiple possible foundational models supporting this conclusion.

title: Quantum battery optimized by parametric amplification
summary: The parametric amplification enabled by two-photon driving constitutes a versatile platform for advanced quantum technologies. We present an optimized scheme for implementing quantum batteries (QBs) based on a superconducting circuit system, where a two-photon-driven LC resonator serves as the charger and an array of transmon qubits functions as the battery. Our results show that two-photon parametric driving exponentially enhances the effective cavity-qubit coupling, which in turn gives rise to near-degenerate energy-level structures and highly entangled quantum states. This significantly enhances the charging power and enables rapid energy transfer from the charger to the battery. Moreover, the engineered squeezed cavity mode and the associated quantum correlations effectively suppress environmentally induced decoherence, thereby delaying energy leakage and facilitating stable energy storage. The proposed scheme remains robust against practical experimental imperfections, such as parameter disorder and environmental noise, preserving its performance advantages. The work provides a feasible platform for realizing high-power, high-stability QBs and highlights the potential of parametric control in quantum energy technologies.

AI.tldr: A superconducting circuit quantum battery using two-photon-driven parametric amplification is proposed, achieving exponentially enhanced charging power, suppressed decoherence, and robust energy storage against experimental imperfections.
AI.motivation: To develop a high-power, high-stability quantum battery platform by leveraging parametric amplification in superconducting circuits, addressing limitations in charging speed and energy storage duration in existing quantum battery schemes.
AI.method: The scheme employs a two-photon-driven LC resonator as a charger coupled to an array of transmon qubits as a battery, utilizing parametric driving to enhance effective cavity-qubit coupling and generate squeezed cavity modes for decoherence suppression.
AI.result: Two-photon parametric driving exponentially enhances effective cavity-qubit coupling, creating near-degenerate energy-level structures and highly entangled states; this significantly boosts charging power and enables rapid energy transfer. Squeezed cavity modes and quantum correlations suppress decoherence, delaying energy leakage.
AI.conclusion: The proposed superconducting circuit quantum battery is robust against parameter disorder and environmental noise, offering a feasible platform for high-power, high-stability quantum energy storage and highlighting parametric control's potential in quantum energy technologies.

title: Fraxonium: Fractional fluxon states for qudit encoding
summary: We propose a superconducting circuit hosting $d$ low-lying states, well separated from the rest of the spectrum, that naturally realizes a qudit system protected from leakage errors. The system represents a generalization of the fluxonium and the low-energy states are constituted by fractional fluxon states, that we call {\it fraxons}, localized in the minima of a suitably designed Josephson potential. The latter is tailored through a Fourier engineering approach, that employs multi-harmonic Josephson building block elements composed by a Josephson junction and an inductance connected in series. We present the spectrum of a $d=4$ and a $d=5$ qudit system and study in detail the qutrit case. We analyze the dipole matrix elements for coupling to radiation and propose a non-Abelian, stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) protocol for single-qutrit gates, that is particularly suited for the present system. The proposed platform opens novel perspectives in circuit engineering and quantum computing beyond the qubit paradigm.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting circuit that naturally realizes a qudit (d-level quantum system) with protection from leakage errors, using fractional fluxon states (fraxons) in a multi-harmonic Josephson potential. It demonstrates d=4 and d=5 qudit systems, studies the qutrit case in detail, and proposes a non-Abelian STIRAP protocol for single-qutrit gates.
AI.motivation: To develop a qudit system that is inherently protected from leakage errors, extending beyond the standard qubit paradigm for quantum computing.
AI.method: A superconducting circuit based on a generalized fluxonium design, using Fourier engineering with multi-harmonic Josephson building blocks (Josephson junction + inductance in series) to create a tailored Josephson potential with d low-lying fractional fluxon states (fraxons).
AI.result: Demonstrated spectra for d=4 and d=5 qudit systems; detailed analysis of the qutrit case; characterized dipole matrix elements for coupling to radiation; proposed a non-Abelian STIRAP protocol for single-qutrit gates.
AI.conclusion: The proposed fraxon-based platform opens new possibilities for circuit engineering and quantum computing beyond the qubit paradigm, offering natural protection against leakage errors.

title: Adaptive Window Decoding based on Spatiotemporal Complementary Gap
summary: Real-time decoding plays a crucial role in practical fault-tolerant quantum computing. Window decoding, in which the decoding problem is divided into windows, is a promising approach. While reducing the window size is desirable for faster decoding, each window contains a buffer region whose size must typically be at least the code distance to avoid degrading the logical error rate, which limits how much the window can shrink. In this paper, we propose an adaptive decoding scheme in which window decoding is first performed with a small buffer size and a decoding confidence (soft information) is computed; if the confidence is low, the buffer size is enlarged and decoding is redone. This approach reduces the average decoding time, since most shots are decoded with a small buffer. A central challenge in realizing this scheme is that existing forms of soft information are not directly applicable to window decoding, especially with a small buffer. We address this challenge by introducing a new form of soft information, the spatiotemporal complementary gap, specifically designed for this setting. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme reduces the average buffer size by approximately 40% while maintaining the logical error rate.

AI.tldr: An adaptive window decoding scheme for quantum error correction uses a small buffer with confidence-based re-decoding, reducing average buffer size by ~40% without degrading logical error rate, enabled by a novel soft information metric called the spatiotemporal complementary gap.
AI.motivation: Real-time decoding is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but window decoding requires a buffer region at least the code distance, limiting how much windows can shrink and thus decoding speed.
AI.method: Proposes adaptive window decoding: decode with small buffer, compute decoding confidence via a new soft information metric (spatiotemporal complementary gap), and re-decode with enlarged buffer only when confidence is low.
AI.result: Numerical simulations show the adaptive scheme reduces average buffer size by approximately 40% while maintaining the logical error rate.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive window decoding with spatiotemporal complementary gap enables faster average decoding by using small buffers most of the time, only enlarging when necessary, without sacrificing error correction performance.

title: Perfect transmission and parallel composition for quantum walks on graphs with two leads
summary: We study scattering for continuous-time quantum walks on finite graphs with two attached leads. We derive explicit formulae for the two-terminal scattering matrix in terms of characteristic polynomials of the finite graph and its vertex-deleted subgraphs. For real-weighted two-terminal graphs, we then introduce three real quantities, $μ_1$, $μ_2$, and $ν$, which are each additive under parallel composition of graphs. In these variables, perfect transmission at fixed momentum is characterized by the condition $μ_1=μ_2$ together with a hyperbola in the corresponding $(μ,ν)$-plane, whose points determine the transmission phase. This turns the search for graphs with prescribed transmission properties into a geometric vector-sum problem for smaller building blocks.

AI.tldr: This paper studies scattering in continuous-time quantum walks on finite graphs with two leads, deriving explicit scattering matrix formulas via characteristic polynomials. For real-weighted two-terminal graphs, three additive quantities (μ₁, μ₂, ν) are introduced, where perfect transmission at fixed momentum is characterized by μ₁=μ₂ and a hyperbola condition in the (μ,ν)-plane, reducing graph design to a geometric vector-sum problem.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic framework for understanding and designing quantum transport properties in finite graphs with leads, particularly by finding additive invariants that simplify the analysis of perfect transmission.
AI.method: Derives explicit two-terminal scattering matrix formulas using characteristic polynomials of the graph and its vertex-deleted subgraphs. Introduces three real additive quantities (μ₁, μ₂, ν) under parallel composition, and characterizes perfect transmission via the conditions μ₁=μ₂ and a hyperbola in the (μ,ν)-plane.
AI.result: Perfect transmission at fixed momentum is characterized by μ₁=μ₂ together with a hyperbola in the (μ,ν)-plane, whose points determine the transmission phase. This reduces the search for graphs with prescribed transmission properties to a geometric vector-sum problem for smaller building blocks.
AI.conclusion: The additive quantities enable a modular, geometric approach to constructing graphs with desired quantum transmission properties via parallel composition of smaller building blocks.

title: Generating Non-Decomposable Maps with Differentiable Semidefinite Programming
summary: Positive maps that are not decomposable are a key resource in entanglement theory because they can detect bound entangled states, yet systematic methods for constructing them remain limited. We introduce an optimization framework based on differentiable semidefinite programming (SDP) for generating positive non-decomposable maps under flexible structural constraints on their Choi matrices. The method combines SDP-based certificates of non-decomposability and positivity with gradient-based optimization, enabling a systematic search over maps with different input and output dimensions. Within this framework, we generate previously unknown numerical examples, identify a parametrized family of maps arising from masked Choi matrices, and construct real non-decomposable maps. We further show that the same approach can be adapted to explore open questions in quantum information theory, including the PPT square conjecture and recently proposed eigenvalue bounds for 2-positive trace-preserving maps.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a differentiable SDP optimization framework to systematically generate positive non-decomposable maps—key for detecting bound entanglement—and produces new numerical examples, parametrized families, and real non-decomposable maps, while also addressing open problems like the PPT square conjecture.
AI.motivation: Positive non-decomposable maps are crucial for detecting bound entangled states, but systematic construction methods are limited, motivating a flexible optimization-based approach.
AI.method: The framework combines differentiable semidefinite programming (SDP) with certificates of positivity and non-decomposability, using gradient-based optimization to search over maps with varying input/output dimensions.
AI.result: Generated previously unknown numerical examples, identified a parametrized family from masked Choi matrices, constructed real non-decomposable maps, and adapted the approach to explore the PPT square conjecture and eigenvalue bounds for 2-positive trace-preserving maps.
AI.conclusion: The differentiable SDP framework provides a systematic and flexible tool for constructing positive non-decomposable maps and investigating open problems in quantum information theory.

title: Blind Quantum Computation on a Modular Superconducting Processor
summary: Current cloud-based quantum processors offer access to advanced hardware hosted on a remote server, but do not guarantee data or algorithm privacy. Blind quantum computation provides information-theoretic privacy by enabling a client to execute an algorithm without disclosing information about either the task or the final result. Here, we execute a measurement-based blind quantum computation protocol on a superconducting processor comprising two flip-chip-bonded modules, one acting as a server and the other as a client. The server generates a two-dimensional cluster state and forwards it to the client. Using this resource, the client implements a universal gate set with only adaptive single-qubit rotations and measurements. To illustrate this approach, we execute a three-qubit instance of the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm. We analyze the server's quantum state after each rotation of a measurement-based single-qubit gate to verify that negligible information about the computation is revealed to the server, consistent with the one-way flow of information that guarantees blindness. This proof-of-principle demonstration establishes key elements of blind quantum computation in superconducting-circuit architectures, indicating that intermediate-scale implementations of blind protocols may become feasible with realistic near-term improvements in gate fidelities.

AI.tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a measurement-based blind quantum computation protocol on a superconducting quantum processor, using two flip-chip-bonded modules (server and client). The server generates a 2D cluster state, and the client performs adaptive single-qubit rotations and measurements to implement a universal gate set with information-theoretic privacy. A three-qubit Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm is executed, and the server's quantum state analysis confirms negligible information leakage, validating the blindness property.
AI.motivation: Current cloud-based quantum processors do not guarantee data or algorithm privacy. Blind quantum computation offers information-theoretic privacy, but practical implementations on superconducting architectures have been lacking.
AI.method: A measurement-based blind quantum computation protocol is implemented on a superconducting processor consisting of two flip-chip-bonded modules. The server generates a two-dimensional cluster state and sends it to the client, who performs only adaptive single-qubit rotations and measurements to achieve a universal gate set. The blindness is verified by analyzing the server's quantum state after each rotation of a measurement-based single-qubit gate.
AI.result: Successfully executed a three-qubit instance of the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm. Analysis of the server's quantum state confirmed that negligible information about the computation is revealed, consistent with the one-way information flow guaranteeing blindness.
AI.conclusion: This proof-of-principle demonstration establishes key elements of blind quantum computation in superconducting-circuit architectures. With near-term improvements in gate fidelities, intermediate-scale implementations of blind protocols may become feasible.

title: Decoherence of $q-$Deformed Photon Added Coherent State
summary: In this study, we explore the behavior of photon added coherent states in a deformed harmonic oscillator subjected to dissipative decoherence. We use $q-$deformation as our nonlinear function to model our system. By adjusting the deformation parameter, we show that $q-$deformed photon added coherent state (DPACS) exhibit greater nonclassicality and resilience to decoherence compared to those of a standard harmonic oscillator. Additionally, we investigate the nonclassical properties and entanglement of DPACS under decoherence induced by interaction with a dissipative photon-loss environment.

AI.tldr: This paper studies photon added coherent states in a q-deformed harmonic oscillator with dissipative decoherence, showing that q-deformation enhances nonclassicality and resilience to decoherence compared to standard oscillators.
AI.motivation: To explore how q-deformation affects the nonclassical properties and decoherence resilience of photon added coherent states in a dissipative environment.
AI.method: The system is modeled using q-deformation as the nonlinear function, with photon added coherent states introduced into a deformed harmonic oscillator. Decoherence is studied via interaction with a dissipative photon-loss environment.
AI.result: q-deformed photon added coherent states (DPACS) exhibit greater nonclassicality and stronger resilience to decoherence than those of a standard harmonic oscillator.
AI.conclusion: q-deformation enhances the robustness and nonclassical features of photon added coherent states against environmental decoherence.

title: A Toolbox to Understand the Physics of Quantum Data Management
summary:
The application of quantum computing to data management has attracted growing interest, yet remains constrained by a limited understanding of how the physical behaviour of quantum devices relates to the structure and difficulty of database problems. In particular, evaluating quantum annealing approaches for combinatorial optimisation, which is central to many data management tasks, poses significant challenges beyond the scope of conventional empirical and complexity-theoretic methods.
  We present a computational toolbox for the systematic numerical analysis of quantum annealing processes derived from data management problem formulations. Adopting a physics-informed perspective, the toolbox enables the study of spectral and dynamical properties -- such as energy gaps and eigenstate structure -- that are inaccessible through direct hardware measurements, yet essential for understanding computational hardness and scaling behaviour.
  Our approach further provides derived quantities and visualisation techniques that support the interpretation of optimisation dynamics, the identification of structural similarities to canonical physical models, and the construction of reduced effective descriptions. By bridging methodological gaps between quantum computing and database systems research, this work establishes a principled foundation for evaluating quantum approaches and guiding future co-design efforts.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a computational toolbox for numerically analyzing quantum annealing processes in data management, focusing on spectral and dynamical properties that explain computational hardness and guide quantum-database co-design.
AI.motivation: There is growing interest in applying quantum computing to data management, but understanding how quantum device physics relates to database problem difficulty remains limited. Conventional empirical and complexity-theoretic methods are insufficient for evaluating quantum annealing approaches to combinatorial optimization problems central to data management.
AI.method: A physics-informed computational toolbox that systematically analyzes spectral properties (energy gaps, eigenstate structure) and dynamical properties of quantum annealing processes derived from data management formulations. Includes derived quantities and visualization techniques for interpreting optimization dynamics, identifying structural similarities to canonical physical models, and constructing reduced effective descriptions.
AI.result: The toolbox enables study of properties inaccessible through direct hardware measurements yet essential for understanding computational hardness and scaling behavior. It bridges methodological gaps between quantum computing and database systems research.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a principled foundation for evaluating quantum approaches to data management problems and guiding future quantum-database co-design efforts.

title: Evolution of Gaussian mixed states under the Markovian master equation for a driven quantum oscillator
summary: We study a generic quantum Markovian master equation for a linearly displaced or driven harmonic oscillator. It was known that the displacement dynamics of Gaussian mixed states depends on the unitary part of the Liouvillian, the decay rate of the system but not on the bath temperature. Here we further show that the fast-rotating modes do not affect the system's displacement dynamics under linear driving forces. Analytical solutions of the quantum master equation are obtained for displaced Gaussian mixed states. Because the non-driven and driven Liouvillians are related by a unitary displacement operator, they are expected to share the same exceptional points structure. At the exceptional points, the displacement of critically damped oscillator displays a characteristics polynomial-in-time prefactor multiplied by an exponential decay. We discuss how external time-dependent forces affect the displacement dynamics using impulsive force and harmonic force as examples. The results obtained for constant driving remain valid in the presence of time-dependent driving.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a quantum Markovian master equation for displaced/driven harmonic oscillators, showing displacement dynamics depend on unitary part and decay rate but not bath temperature. Fast-rotating modes don't affect displacement under linear driving. Analytical solutions for Gaussian mixed states are derived, exceptional points structure is shared between non-driven and driven Liouvillians, and at exceptional points displacement shows polynomial-in-time prefactor with exponential decay. Results for constant driving extend to time-dependent driving.
AI.motivation: To understand how linear displacement or driving affects the dynamics of a quantum harmonic oscillator governed by a Markovian master equation, particularly focusing on displacement dynamics, the role of fast-rotating modes, and the exceptional points structure.
AI.method: Analytical solutions of the quantum Markovian master equation for displaced Gaussian mixed states; analysis using unitary displacement operators relating non-driven and driven Liouvillians; examination of exceptional points and polynomial-in-time prefactors; application of impulsive and harmonic driving forces.
AI.result: Displacement dynamics depend on the unitary part and decay rate but not on bath temperature; fast-rotating modes do not affect displacement under linear driving; non-driven and driven Liouvillians share same exceptional points structure; at exceptional points, critically damped oscillator displacement shows polynomial-in-time prefactor with exponential decay; constant driving results remain valid for time-dependent driving.
AI.conclusion: The displacement dynamics of a linearly driven quantum harmonic oscillator in a Markovian environment are robust to bath temperature and fast-rotating modes, and the exceptional point structure is preserved under driving, with time-dependent forces not altering the fundamental displacement behavior derived for constant driving.

title: Programmable cavity-enhanced telecom quantum memory in thin-film lithium niobate
summary: Spectrally multiplexed telecom quantum networks require quantum memories that combine efficient storage with programmable frequency addressing. An ideal integrated implementation should therefore unite a native telecom transition, efficient storage and fast on-chip spectral control. Here we demonstrate a cavity-enhanced quantum memory in an isotopically purified $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$-doped thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator. Long-lived hyperfine shelving states support persistent, high-contrast atomic frequency comb preparation, with a single-component comb lifetime of $277.6 \pm 52.6$s. Together with cavity impedance matching, this yields an on-chip storage efficiency of $23.3 \pm 0.5\%$ for 100-ns storage. The intrinsic electro-optic response of lithium niobate enables frequency-selective storage and routing of retrieved photons at rates up to 20~MHz with inter-channel crosstalk below $10^{-4}$. We further store and retrieve time-energy-entangled telecom photons, violating an entanglement-witness bound by more than 11 standard deviations and thus verifying the quantum nature of the storage process. Our results establish erbium-doped thin-film lithium niobate as a programmable light--matter interface for spectrally multiplexed quantum networks.

AI.tldr: A cavity-enhanced quantum memory in erbium-doped thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator achieves efficient on-chip storage (23.3% efficiency), long-lived hyperfine shelving (277.6 s comb lifetime), fast electro-optic frequency control (20 MHz routing, <10^{-4} crosstalk), and entanglement-preserving storage verified by 11σ violation of an entanglement witness.
AI.motivation: To realize a programmable light–matter interface for spectrally multiplexed telecom quantum networks that combines native telecom operation, efficient quantum storage, and fast on-chip frequency control in an integrated platform.
AI.method: A cavity-enhanced quantum memory implemented in an isotopically purified ¹⁶⁷Er³⁺-doped thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator, using long-lived hyperfine shelving states for persistent atomic frequency comb preparation and the intrinsic electro-optic effect for frequency-selective control.
AI.result: On-chip storage efficiency of 23.3±0.5% for 100-ns storage, single-component comb lifetime of 277.6±52.6 s, frequency-selective routing at rates up to 20 MHz with inter-channel crosstalk below 10⁻⁴, and entanglement-witness violation by >11σ using time-energy-entangled telecom photons.
AI.conclusion: Erbium-doped thin-film lithium niobate establishes a programmable light–matter interface suitable for spectrally multiplexed quantum networks.

title: The influence of strong coupling between single-photon source and spectral filter on photon statistics
summary: One of the most common approaches for coupling optical single-photon sources and photonic integrated circuits is to use a cavity. The cavity acts as a spectral filter that distorts the light spectrum and changes its statistical properties. But in the general case one should take into account not only spectral filtering of light but also the spectral filter influence on the single-photon source dynamics. We build an effective analytical model for description of the cavity influence on the photon statistics of light emitted by the single-photon source as spectral filtering only. We show that this model correctly describes the photon statistics even in a strong-coupling regime between the single-photon source and the spectral filter. Our results can be useful for analytical modeling of photon statistics of quantum emitters strongly coupled to various electromagnetic interfaces.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an effective analytical model that describes cavity influence on single-photon source as pure spectral filtering, which correctly predicts photon statistics even in strong-coupling regimes.
AI.motivation: Cavities used to couple single-photon sources to photonic circuits act as spectral filters that distort the light spectrum and change its statistical properties. The general case requires accounting for both spectral filtering and its influence on source dynamics, which is complex.
AI.method: The authors build an effective analytical model treating the cavity's influence solely as spectral filtering, and validate it against the strong-coupling regime between the single-photon source and the spectral filter.
AI.result: The model correctly describes photon statistics even in the strong-coupling regime between the single-photon source and the spectral filter.
AI.conclusion: The model is useful for analytical modeling of photon statistics from quantum emitters strongly coupled to various electromagnetic interfaces.

title: The Heisenberg-Weyl-parity group its coherent states and a unified Wigner-Weyl function
summary: The Heisenberg-Weyl group $HW(d)$ related to a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space $H(d)$, is enlarged into the Heisenberg-Weyl-parity group $HWP(d)$ that incorporates parity transformations. It consists of $2d^3$ elements, of which $d^3$ elements belong to the $HW(d)$ subgroup, and extra $d^3$ elements which are related through a Fourier transform with the former ones. It is shown that $HWP(d)$ is a generalised version of the dihedral group. The properties of operators that combine displacements and parity, are discussed. $HWP(d)$ is shown to be a solvable group, and commutators of its elements perform displacement and parity transformations of quantum states, along loops in the discrete phase space.$2d^2$ coherent states related to the $HWP(d)$ group are introduced, which consist of $d^2$ coherent states related to the $HW(d)$ subgroup, and extra $d^2$ coherent states which are related through a Fourier transform with the former ones. In noisy cases, expansion of an arbitrary state in terms of the $2d^2$ coherent states with Bargmann coefficients, is advantageous in comparison to expansion in terms of the $d^2$ coherent states related to $HW(d)$. One of the consequences of the $HWP(d)$ group, is a natural unification of the Wigner and Weyl functions. The properties of the unified Wigner-Weyl function are discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Heisenberg-Weyl-parity group HWP(d) as an enlargement of the Heisenberg-Weyl group HW(d) by incorporating parity transformations, leading to 2d³ elements. It shows HWP(d) is a generalized dihedral group, solvable, and relates to coherent states, noise handling, and a unified Wigner-Weyl function.
AI.motivation: To enlarge the Heisenberg-Weyl group by including parity transformations, thereby creating a richer algebraic structure (HWP(d)) that unifies displacement and parity operations in discrete phase space, and to demonstrate its advantages for quantum state representation and noise resilience.
AI.method: The group HWP(d) is constructed by adding parity-related elements to HW(d), yielding 2d³ elements where the extra d³ elements are Fourier-transformed relatives. Group-theoretic properties (solvability, dihedral generalization) are analyzed. Coherent states (2d²) are introduced, half from HW(d) and half via Fourier transform. The unified Wigner-Weyl function is derived from the group structure.
AI.result: HWP(d) is a solvable group generalizing the dihedral group. Commutators along discrete phase-space loops produce displacement/parity transformations. 2d² coherent states with Bargmann coefficients offer better noise robustness than d² HW(d) coherent states. The Wigner and Weyl functions are naturally unified under HWP(d).
AI.conclusion: The HWP(d) group provides a natural framework unifying parity and displacement operations, leading to improved coherent-state expansions for noisy scenarios and a unified Wigner-Weyl function, offering a more complete toolkit for discrete quantum phase-space analysis.

title: Nonlinear Hamiltonians and Boolean satisfiability
summary: We consider an extended model of quantum computation where a scalable fault-tolerant quantum computer is coupled to one or more ancilla qubits that evolve according to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Following the approach of Abrams and Lloyd, an efficient quantum circuit evaluating an $n$-bit Boolean function in conjunctive normal form is used to prepare an ancilla encoding its number $s$ of satisfying assignments ($0 \le s \le 2^n$). This is followed by a nonlinear quantum state discrimination gate on the ancilla qubit that is used to learn properties of $s$. Here we consider three types of state discriminators generated by different nonlinear Hamiltonians. First, given a restricted Boolean satisfiability problem with the promise of at most one satisfying assignment ($ 0 \le s \le 1$), we show that a qubit with $\langle σ^z \rangle σ^z$ nonlinearity can be used to efficiently determine whether $s = 0$ or $s = 1$, solving the UNIQUE SAT problem. Here $\langle A \rangle := \langle ψ| A |ψ\rangle $ denotes expectation in the current state. UNIQUE SAT is NP-hard under a randomized polynomial-time reduction (of course any discussion of complexity assumes a scalable, fault-tolerant implementation). Second, for unrestricted satisfiability problems with $ 0 \le s \le 2^n$, a Hamiltonian with $ \langle σ^x \rangle σ^y - \langle σ^y \rangle σ^x$ nonlinearity can be used to efficiently determine whether $s=0$ or $s>0$, thereby solving 3SAT, which is NP-complete. Finally, we show that $ \langle σ^y \rangle \langle σ^z \rangle σ^x - \langle σ^x \rangle \langle σ^z \rangle σ^y $ nonlinearity can be used to efficiently measure $s$ and solve #SAT, which is #P-complete. The nonlinear models are of mean field type and might be simulated with ultracold atoms.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that coupling a fault-tolerant quantum computer to nonlinear ancilla qubits (evolving under specific nonlinear Schrödinger equations) can efficiently solve NP-complete problems (UNIQUE SAT, 3SAT) and #P-complete problems (#SAT) via nonlinear quantum state discrimination, using mean-field-type nonlinearities that might be realizable with ultracold atoms.
AI.motivation: To explore whether nonlinear quantum mechanics, when combined with standard fault-tolerant quantum computing, can solve hard computational problems (NP-complete and #P-complete) that are believed intractable for purely linear quantum computation.
AI.method: The authors extend the Abrams-Lloyd framework: a fault-tolerant quantum computer prepares an ancilla qubit whose state encodes the number $s$ of satisfying assignments of an $n$-bit Boolean function. Then, three distinct nonlinear Hamiltonians are applied to the ancilla for state discrimination: (1) $\langle \sigma^z \rangle \sigma^z$ nonlinearity to distinguish $s=0$ vs $s=1$ (UNIQUE SAT); (2) $\langle \sigma^x \rangle \sigma^y - \langle \sigma^y \rangle \sigma^x$ nonlinearity to distinguish $s=0$ vs $s>0$ (3SAT); (3) $\langle \sigma^y \rangle \langle \sigma^z \rangle \sigma^x - \langle \sigma^x \rangle \langle \sigma^z \rangle \sigma^y$ nonlinearity to measure $s$ exactly (#SAT).
AI.result: The nonlinear discrimination gates allow solving UNIQUE SAT (NP-hard under randomized polynomial-time reduction), 3SAT (NP-complete), and #SAT (#P-complete) in polynomial time, assuming a scalable fault-tolerant implementation. The required nonlinearities are of mean-field type and potentially simulable with ultracold atomic systems.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear quantum mechanics, if physically realizable, could dramatically extend the power of quantum computation beyond the standard linear model, allowing efficient solutions to problems in NP and #P. The mean-field-type nonlinear Hamiltonians considered may be amenable to experimental realization with ultracold atoms.

title: Efficient ultrafast homodyne detection of quantum light
summary: Ultrafast continuous-variable quantum states offer new opportunities for advanced quantum technologies, but efficient homodyne detection of these states remains challenging. Here, we present a method for efficient ultrafast homodyne detection by exploiting temporal correlations in detector signals. By optimizing the temporal weight used to extract quadrature outcomes, we achieve a substantial increase in the signal-to-noise ratio of ultrafast homodyne detection, thereby improving the detection efficiency. We analyze the autocorrelations of shot noise and electronic noise and determine the optimal weight by solving a generalized Rayleigh quotient problem. The optimal weight enhances the squeezing and anti-squeezing levels observed experimentally. These results highlight the importance of optimized signal processing for efficient quantum measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method to improve ultrafast homodyne detection efficiency by optimizing temporal weighting of detector signals based on autocorrelation analysis of shot and electronic noise, solving a generalized Rayleigh quotient problem to enhance signal-to-noise ratio and observed squeezing levels.
AI.motivation: Efficient homodyne detection of ultrafast continuous-variable quantum states remains challenging, limiting their application in advanced quantum technologies.
AI.method: The authors exploit temporal correlations in detector signals by optimizing the temporal weight used to extract quadrature outcomes. They analyze autocorrelations of shot noise and electronic noise and determine the optimal weight by solving a generalized Rayleigh quotient problem.
AI.result: The optimized temporal weighting substantially increases the signal-to-noise ratio of ultrafast homodyne detection, thereby improving detection efficiency and enhancing experimentally observed squeezing and anti-squeezing levels.
AI.conclusion: Optimized signal processing is crucial for efficient quantum measurements, and the proposed method demonstrates a practical path to improve ultrafast homodyne detection performance.

title: Nonlocal Topological Maxwell Demon Teleporting Ergotropy via Surface-Code Quantum Error Correction
summary: We introduce a nonlocal Maxwell demon teleporting ergotropy at finite temperature via classical communication and a shared surface code. The teleported ergotropy is exponentially protected below a topological threshold. We identify a thermodynamic phase transition separating a profitable demon phase from a thermal phase. A quadratic infrastructure cost strictly enforces the second law, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic horizon on separation distance. This establishes quantum error correction as a resource for nonlocal thermodynamics beyond fault-tolerant computation.

AI.tldr: A nonlocal Maxwell demon uses a shared surface code and classical communication to teleport ergotropy (usable work) at finite temperature, with exponential protection below a topological threshold. A thermodynamic phase transition separates profitable and thermal phases, and a quadratic infrastructure cost enforces the second law, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic horizon on distance. This establishes QEC as a resource for nonlocal thermodynamics beyond fault-tolerant computation.
AI.motivation: To explore whether quantum error correction (specifically surface codes) can serve as a resource for nonlocal thermodynamic tasks—enabling the teleportation of ergotropy (usable work) at finite temperature—and to understand the fundamental limits imposed by thermodynamics on such processes.
AI.method: The authors introduce a nonlocal Maxwell demon model that employs classical communication and a shared surface code to teleport ergotropy. They analyze the protocol at finite temperature, studying its performance in terms of topological protection below a threshold, and derive the thermodynamic costs (e.g., a quadratic infrastructure cost) that enforce the second law.
AI.result: The teleported ergotropy is exponentially protected below a topological threshold. A thermodynamic phase transition is identified between a profitable demon phase and a thermal phase. A quadratic infrastructure cost strictly enforces the second law, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic horizon on the separation distance over which teleportation remains viable.
AI.conclusion: Quantum error correction is established as a resource for nonlocal thermodynamics beyond its traditional role in fault-tolerant quantum computation, revealing a fundamental trade-off between thermodynamic profitability and spatial separation.

title: Sharp Bounds on the Eigenvalues of Kikuchi Graphs and Applications to Quantum Max Cut
summary:
We prove that the maximum eigenvalue of the (both signed and unsigned) Laplacian of level $k$ Kikuchi graph of any graph $G$ with $m$ edges is at most $m+k$. This confirms four recent conjectures of Apte, Parekh, and Sud.
  As applications, we obtain that tensor products of one and two qubit product states achieve an approximation ratio of $5/8$ for Quantum Max Cut and $5/7$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Moreover, combining our bounds with the algorithms analyzed by Apte, Parekh, and Sud, yields efficient algorithms achieving an approximation ratio of $0.614$ for Quantum Max Cut and $0.674$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Finally, we also make modest progress on Brouwer's conjecture and improve Lew's bound on the sum of the top-$k$ eigenvalues of a Graph Laplacian.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the maximum eigenvalue of Laplacians for level-k Kikuchi graphs is at most m+k, confirming four conjectures. Applications include improved approximation ratios for Quantum Max Cut and XY Hamiltonian, progress on Brouwer's conjecture, and improved bounds on top-k eigenvalues of Graph Laplacians.
AI.motivation: To confirm four recent conjectures by Apte, Parekh, and Sud regarding eigenvalue bounds of Kikuchi graph Laplacians, and to derive improved approximation algorithms for quantum Hamiltonian problems.
AI.method: The authors prove eigenvalue bounds for both signed and unsigned Laplacians of level-k Kikuchi graphs. They apply these bounds to analyze approximation ratios for tensor product states in Quantum Max Cut and XY Hamiltonian, and combine with existing algorithms for better ratios. They also apply the techniques to Brouwer's conjecture and Lew's bound.
AI.result: Maximum eigenvalue ≤ m+k for Kikuchi graph Laplacians. Tensor product states achieve 5/8 for Quantum Max Cut and 5/7 for XY Hamiltonian. Combined with existing algorithms yields 0.614 for Quantum Max Cut and 0.674 for XY Hamiltonian. Modest progress on Brouwer's conjecture; improved Lew's bound on sum of top-k graph Laplacian eigenvalues.
AI.conclusion: The proven eigenvalue bounds resolve four open conjectures and yield concrete improvements for quantum approximation algorithms, as well as advances in spectral graph theory.

title: Majorana Constellations: A Geometric Lens on Multipartite Entanglement and Geometric Phases
summary: The Majorana stellar representation translates abstract quantum spin states into intuitive geometric constellations on the Bloch sphere, revealing symmetries, degeneracies, and correlations that traditional algebraic methods often obscure. Within quantum information science, this framework provides a powerful lens for characterizing symmetric multi-qubit and higher-spin systems. By encoding entanglement directly into spatial coordinates, the constellation geometry yields exact measures of concurrence, three-tangle, and genuine multipartite entanglement, while its dynamical evolution uncovers internal anomalous contributions to geometric phases. While interest in stellar representations has resurged, existing literature remains fragmented, lacking a unified treatment of these entanglement-specific metrics and their higher-dimensional dynamics. This review synthesizes the entanglement-centric perspective on Majorana representations, bridging discrete algebraic classifications (e.g., SLOCC orbits) with continuous geometric interpretations. Crucially, we highlight how this framework circumvents \#P-hard computational bottlenecks, leveraging polynomial-time tractability to evaluate multipartite invariants. We detail the interplay between constellation topology and higher-spin Berry/Hannay phases, explore extensions beyond pure symmetric states, and review applications in quantum metrology, state engineering, and condensed-matter physics. By foregrounding entanglement as the unifying theme, this comprehensive examination establishes Majorana stars as a fundamental geometric language, uniquely positioned to inspire new theoretical and experimental directions in quantum technologies.

AI.tldr: This review synthesizes the Majorana stellar representation as a geometric framework for quantum spin states, showing how constellation geometry on the Bloch sphere provides exact entanglement measures (concurrence, three-tangle, genuine multipartite entanglement), polynomial-time tractability for otherwise #P-hard invariants, and links to geometric phases, while bridging SLOCC classifications with continuous geometric interpretations for applications in quantum metrology, state engineering, and condensed matter.
AI.motivation: Existing literature on Majorana stellar representations remains fragmented and lacks a unified treatment of entanglement-specific metrics and higher-dimensional dynamics, despite renewed interest in the framework.
AI.method: The authors synthesize an entanglement-centric perspective on Majorana representations, bridging discrete algebraic classifications (e.g., SLOCC orbits) with continuous geometric interpretations, and leveraging polynomial-time tractability to circumvent #P-hard computational bottlenecks for multipartite invariants.
AI.result: The framework yields exact geometric measures of concurrence, three-tangle, and genuine multipartite entanglement; reveals internal anomalous contributions to geometric phases from dynamical evolution; and enables polynomial-time evaluation of otherwise #P-hard multipartite invariants.
AI.conclusion: By foregrounding entanglement as the unifying theme, Majorana stars are established as a fundamental geometric language uniquely positioned to inspire new theoretical and experimental directions in quantum technologies.

title: A Resource-Driven Framework for Configurable Entanglement in Quantum Networks
comment: This work has been funded by the European Union under the ERC grant QNattyNet, n. 101169850
summary: Shared multipartite entanglement defines a ``whatever channel'', i.e., a latent communication substrate that does not determine a priori which end-to-end entangled links are activated, but can be configured to support different entanglement-connectivity graphs through Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC). Building on this, we propose a resource-driven framework in which multipartite entanglement is treated as a programmable resource that induces a space of admissible entanglement-graph configurations. Within this framework, connectivity provisioning emerges as a particular instance of a more general resource reconfiguration process. To support this paradigm, we introduce a set of structural design parameters that characterize the operational degrees of freedom of the resource and define the admissible transformations independently of the specific mechanism used to realize them. We then formalize Entanglement Rolling as a measurement-based protocol that operates over the induced configuration space, enabling the systematic reconfiguration of the shared resource across a family of multipartite states. Finally, we analyze the proposed framework under realistic noise conditions. Leveraging the Noisy Stabilizer Formalism (NSF), we derive closed-form noise maps that characterize the effect of noise on the resource transformations and show that the proposed approach maintains reliable performance under relevant noise processes.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a framework for shared multipartite entanglement as a programmable "whatever channel" that can be reconfigured via LOCC to support different entanglement-connectivity graphs. It defines structural design parameters, proposes Entanglement Rolling as a measurement-based reconfiguration protocol, and analyzes performance under noise using the Noisy Stabilizer Formalism.
AI.motivation: To treat multipartite entanglement as a programmable resource that can be reconfigured to support different entanglement-connectivity graphs, rather than predetermining which end-to-end entangled links are activated.
AI.method: Proposes a resource-driven framework with structural design parameters, introduces Entanglement Rolling as a measurement-based protocol operating over an induced configuration space, and analyzes noise resilience using the Noisy Stabilizer Formalism (NSF) to derive closed-form noise maps.
AI.result: The framework enables systematic reconfiguration of shared multipartite entanglement across a family of states, with closed-form NSF-derived noise maps showing reliable performance under realistic noise conditions.
AI.conclusion: Connectivity provisioning can be viewed as an instance of resource reconfiguration, and the Entanglement Rolling protocol provides a viable measurement-based approach that maintains performance under noise.

title: Excitation Flow, Positivity, and Fisher Information for Open Subsystems of an $N$-Qubit Network
summary: We derive closed-form propagators for any $K$-qubit subsystem of a closed $N$-qubit network with a single conserved excitation. A single transition amplitude simultaneously controls excitation flow between subsystems, the positivity and complete positivity of every propagator, the entanglement entropy of every subsystem, and the quantum Fisher information for global parameters. Positivity and complete positivity coincide, determined solely by the direction of excitation flow, independently of subsystem size, coherence, or entanglement structure. A propagator is positive and completely positive if and only if it contracts the subsystem state toward its fixed point. The ensemble of propagators collectively constrains global properties inaccessible to any single subsystem. For single-qubit subsystems, we characterize the ensemble's fixed-point distribution and domain of positivity, finding a band of states that lies inside the positivity domain of every propagator yet is never visited by the physical dynamics. The quantum Fisher information decomposes into state and process contributions over any observation window $[t_1,t_2]$, with the state contribution bounded while the process contribution grows secularly. The total Fisher information is minimal when all future propagators are nonpositive and not completely positive, and near its maximum when they are positive and completely positive.

AI.tldr: This paper derives closed-form propagators for K-qubit subsystems in an N-qubit network with a single conserved excitation, showing that positivity and complete positivity of propagators are determined solely by excitation flow direction. It characterizes fixed-point distributions, identifies a "band of states" never visited by physical dynamics, and decomposes quantum Fisher information into state and process contributions with distinct scaling behaviors.
AI.motivation: To understand the fundamental constraints governing quantum information propagation in multi-qubit networks with conserved excitations, particularly the relationship between subsystem propagator properties (positivity, complete positivity) and global quantum metrological resources.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of closed-form propagators for K-qubit subsystems via symmetry reduction from the conserved-excitation constraint; analysis of positivity/complete positivity conditions; decomposition of quantum Fisher information into state and process contributions over observation windows.
AI.result: (1) Positivity and complete positivity coincide for all subsystem propagators and are solely determined by excitation flow direction. (2) A propagator is positive/completely positive iff it contracts toward its fixed point. (3) There exists a band of states inside every propagator's positivity domain that is never visited by dynamics. (4) Quantum Fisher information decomposes into bounded state contribution and secularly growing process contribution; total Fisher information is minimal when propagators are nonpositive and maximal when they are positive/completely positive.
AI.conclusion: Subsystem propagator positivity is a simple function of excitation flow direction, decoupled from subsystem size or coherence. The ensemble of propagators imposes collective constraints on global dynamics. The Fisher information decomposition reveals how process contributions dominate long-time metrological sensitivity.

title: Deforming the Trail: Baseline Quantum Circuitry for $\text{SU(2)}_k$ Lattice Gauge Theory
summary: Quantifying quantum resources for simulating the fundamental forces of Nature is sensitive to the mapping of gauge fields onto finite quantum computational architectures. When locally truncating lattice gauge theories in the irreducible representation basis, it has been proposed to further deform the theory via quantum groups. The purpose of this deformation is (1) to provide an infinite tower of finite-dimensional ($d = k+1$) groups systematically approximating the infinite-dimensional gauge links and (2) to restore the physical unitarity of a plaquette operator diagonalization procedure analytically derived from the field continuum by recontracting vertex pairs. For the SU(2)$_k$ Yang-Mills pure-gauge theory, we provide a constructive strategy of gauge-variant completions to extend this unitarity to the entire computational Hilbert space, leading to well-defined time evolution unitaries as targets for optimized circuit synthesis. Leveraging basic circuit decompositions and symmetries of the diagonalized plaquette operator, we report resource upper-bounds on the generalized-controlled-X two-qudit gates for arbitrary local truncation $d$, reducing estimates and scaling relative to the non-deformed theory by three polynomial powers from $O(d^8)$ to $O(d^5)$. Examining the stronger q-deformed gauge constraint, which softens the total flux at vertices, we show that the physical Hilbert space dimension of the deformed plaquette operator scales equivalently to its non-deformed counterpart with a constant factor $0.2563(5)$. Thus, despite affecting interactions at all scales as exemplified by the observed flux hierarchy inversion symmetry, q-deformation continues to pass scrutiny as a reliable truncation offering advantages in quantum circuit synthesis.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a gauge-variant completion strategy for SU(2)$_k$ Yang-Mills theory to restore physical unitarity in deformed lattice gauge theories using quantum groups. It reports improved resource upper-bounds for quantum circuit synthesis from $O(d^8)$ to $O(d^5)$ and shows that the physical Hilbert space dimension scales equivalently to the non-deformed case with a constant factor of $0.2563(5)$, confirming q-deformation as a reliable truncation for quantum simulation.
AI.motivation: To systematically approximate infinite-dimensional gauge links in lattice gauge theories with finite-dimensional quantum computational architectures while restoring physical unitarity that is analytically derived from the continuum.
AI.method: Constructive gauge-variant completions for SU(2)$_k$ Yang-Mills pure-gauge theory, leveraging circuit decompositions and symmetries of diagonalized plaquette operators to derive resource upper-bounds and scaling analysis.
AI.result: Resource upper-bounds on generalized-controlled-X two-qudit gates reduced from $O(d^8)$ to $O(d^5)$. Physical Hilbert space dimension of the deformed plaquette operator scales equivalently to non-deformed with constant factor $0.2563(5)$.
AI.conclusion: Q-deformation remains a reliable truncation method offering advantages in quantum circuit synthesis despite affecting interactions at all scales via flux hierarchy inversion symmetry.

title: Transient dynamics of parametric driving for single-electron image current detection in a Paul trap
summary: Nondestructive detection of single-electron motion is crucial for quantum information processing with electrons trapped in Paul traps. The standard approach in Penning traps is to detect the image current induced on the trap electrodes by the electron's oscillatory motion. However, applying this approach in Paul traps for single electrons is currently hindered by motional frequency fluctuations arising from trap anharmonicities and instabilities in the rf trapping field. In this work, we propose a robust detection scheme exploiting the transient dynamics of parametric driving to overcome these limitations. Distinct from traditional steady-state approaches, our method focuses on the transient regime to break the temporal constraints imposed by steady-state assumptions, thereby enabling fast readout. We show that a controlled ramp of the parametric drive effectively locks the frequency of the electron motion in the transient regime, rendering the signal highly resilient to realistic experimental noise and inherent micromotion. This work paves the way for the experimental realization of nondestructive detection of single-electron motion in Paul traps.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a robust detection scheme using transient parametric driving to enable nondestructive single-electron motion detection in Paul traps, overcoming frequency fluctuation issues caused by anharmonicities and rf field instabilities.
AI.motivation: Nondestructive detection of single-electron motion is crucial for quantum information processing with trapped electrons, but the standard image-current detection approach used in Penning traps is hindered in Paul traps by motional frequency fluctuations from trap anharmonicities and rf trapping field instabilities.
AI.method: A robust detection scheme exploiting transient dynamics of parametric driving. Instead of traditional steady-state approaches, the method focuses on the transient regime to break temporal constraints. A controlled ramp of the parametric drive locks the electron motion frequency in the transient regime, making the signal resilient to experimental noise and micromotion.
AI.result: The transient parametric driving scheme renders the detection signal highly resilient to realistic experimental noise and inherent micromotion, enabling fast readout that overcomes the limitations of steady-state approaches.
AI.conclusion: This work paves the way for the experimental realization of nondestructive detection of single-electron motion in Paul traps.

title: Energy efficiency of quantum computers
summary: How much energy does a quantum computer consume? Are they more efficient than their classical counterparts? In this work, we make a step towards answering these questions. We define the energy efficiency of a quantum computer as the ratio of the number of algorithms it can perform during a given time over the energy consumed by the hardware during this time. We analyze the most representative physical platforms currently envisioned to be used as building blocks of quantum computers: superconducting qubits, silicon spin qubits, trapped ions, neutral atoms and photonic qubits. Including insights from experts in all these technologies and taking into account algorithm compilation constraints, we discuss the advantages and inconveniences of each platform from an energy standpoint. Beyond providing concrete values of the energy consumption of current quantum computers, we lay the foundation of a framework to benchmark the energy efficiency of any future quantum computing architecture.

AI.tldr: This paper defines and benchmarks the energy efficiency of quantum computers across five hardware platforms (superconducting qubits, silicon spin qubits, trapped ions, neutral atoms, photonic qubits), providing concrete energy consumption values and a framework for comparing future quantum architectures against classical counterparts.
AI.motivation: To answer whether quantum computers are more energy-efficient than classical computers by defining energy efficiency metrics and analyzing the energy consumption of leading quantum hardware platforms.
AI.method: The study defines energy efficiency as the ratio of algorithms performed per unit time over energy consumed. It analyzes five major qubit platforms (superconducting, silicon spin, trapped ions, neutral atoms, photonic) using expert insights and algorithm compilation constraints.
AI.result: Provides concrete energy consumption values for current quantum computers across different platforms, along with advantages and disadvantages of each from an energy standpoint.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a foundational benchmarking framework for evaluating the energy efficiency of any future quantum computing architecture, enabling systematic comparison with classical computers.

title: Accelerating State-Vector Quantum Simulation on Integrated GPUs via Cache Locality Optimization: A Cross-Architecture Evaluation
summary: The classical simulation of quantum algorithms is a crucial tool for circuit development, testing, and validation. Although acceleration using GPUs significantly reduces simulation time, most high-performance simulators rely on vendor-specific frameworks that target data-center hardware. To broaden access to quantum simulation, this work proposes a vendor-agnostic approach targeting the integrated GPUs commonly found in consumer-grade laptops. A primary challenge in state-vector simulation is its inherently poor spatial locality, which creates a memory bandwidth bottleneck. Consequently, baseline implementations experience a severe degradation in relative GPU speedup as the number of simulated qubits increases. To address this limitation, we introduce a state partitioning optimization that reorganizes the quantum state vector to maximize the last-level cache locality and minimize costly main memory fetches. We evaluate this strategy using a Quantum Phase Estimation algorithm across diverse architectures from Intel, AMD, and Apple. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed optimization successfully mitigates performance degradation at larger qubit scales. In particular, for a 28-qubit simulation, the optimization reversed a performance deficit on an Intel Core i5, improving the GPU speedup over the CPU from 0.95x to 1.89x, and increased the Apple M1 Pro speedup from 3.71x to 5.88x. Overall, this approach yields consistent execution time improvements, demonstrating the viability of integrated GPUs for efficient quantum circuit simulation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a vendor-agnostic approach for quantum circuit simulation on integrated GPUs (common in consumer laptops) and introduces a state partitioning optimization to improve cache locality. The method is evaluated on Intel, AMD, and Apple architectures, showing significant GPU speedup improvements, e.g., from 0.95x to 1.89x on an Intel Core i5 and from 3.71x to 5.88x on Apple M1 Pro for 28-qubit simulations.
AI.motivation: Classical simulation of quantum algorithms is essential for circuit development and validation. Most high-performance simulators rely on vendor-specific frameworks targeting data-center GPUs, limiting accessibility. This work aims to broaden access by targeting integrated GPUs in consumer-grade laptops.
AI.method: A vendor-agnostic approach is proposed that targets integrated GPUs. To address the memory bandwidth bottleneck caused by poor spatial locality in state-vector simulation, a state partitioning optimization is introduced that reorganizes the quantum state vector to maximize last-level cache locality and minimize main memory fetches.
AI.result: Evaluation using Quantum Phase Estimation on Intel, AMD, and Apple architectures shows the optimization mitigates performance degradation at larger qubit scales. For a 28-qubit simulation, GPU speedup improved from 0.95x to 1.89x on Intel Core i5 and from 3.71x to 5.88x on Apple M1 Pro.
