AI.conclusion: The proposed state partitioning optimization yields consistent execution time improvements, demonstrating that integrated GPUs in consumer laptops are viable for efficient quantum circuit simulation.

title: Scalable self-testing of generic multipartite quantum states
summary: Characterizing large quantum systems with minimal assumptions is a central challenge in quantum information science. Self-testing provides the strongest form of certification by identifying the underlying quantum state solely from observed measurement statistics. However, existing self-testing methods for generic $n$-partite states face a scalability barrier, requiring exponentially many samples in the system size. In this work, we overcome this barrier by introducing a protocol that robustly self-tests almost all $n$-qubit states with only polynomial sample complexity. The key ingredient is an efficient scheme for device-independently evaluating multipartite Pauli measurements, which can be implemented using only a linear number of ancillary Bell pairs together with standard projective and Bell measurements, well within the reach of current quantum technology. Beyond self-testing states, our scheme provides a general framework for implementing a wide range of learning and certification protocols in the device-independent setting, thereby opening a scalable route to device-independent quantum information processing in large-scale quantum networks.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a scalable protocol that robustly self-tests almost all n-qubit states with only polynomial sample complexity, overcoming the exponential scalability barrier of existing methods, using a device-independent scheme for multipartite Pauli measurements requiring only a linear number of ancillary Bell pairs.
AI.motivation: Existing self-testing methods for generic n-partite states require exponentially many samples, creating a scalability barrier for characterizing large quantum systems with minimal assumptions in a device-independent manner.
AI.method: The protocol introduces an efficient scheme for device-independently evaluating multipartite Pauli measurements, implemented using a linear number of ancillary Bell pairs combined with standard projective and Bell measurements, achieving polynomial sample complexity for robustly self-testing almost all n-qubit states.
AI.result: Overcomes the exponential scalability barrier by achieving polynomial sample complexity for self-testing almost all n-qubit states, with the protocol implementable within current quantum technology.
AI.conclusion: The scheme provides a general framework for device-independent learning and certification protocols, enabling scalable device-independent quantum information processing in large-scale quantum networks.

title: New approaches to almost i.i.d. information theory
summary: Independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) states are ubiquitous in quantum information theory. However, in a practical setting, the i.i.d. assumption is too stringent, and possibly not realistic. A physically more compelling class of 'almost i.i.d.' sources was recently proposed by [Mazzola/Sutter/Renner, arXiv:2603.15792]. In this paper, we introduce two alternative definitions of almost i.i.d. states, based on the normalised quantum Wasserstein distance and on the idea of looking at the average $k$-body marginal. We explore some basic properties of these notions and prove a strict hierarchical relation among them, with Mazzola et al.'s notion being the strictest, the one based on $k$-body marginals the loosest, and the one based on the quantum Wasserstein distance in between. Strict separation is established by means of explicit examples.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes two new definitions of "almost i.i.d." quantum states—one based on normalized quantum Wasserstein distance and another on average k-body marginals—and establishes a strict hierarchy among these and a prior definition by Mazzola et al., showing explicit separation examples.
AI.motivation: The i.i.d. assumption in quantum information theory is often unrealistic for practical settings; the authors aim to provide more physically meaningful definitions of "almost i.i.d." states and understand their relationships.
AI.method: Two alternative definitions are introduced: one using the normalized quantum Wasserstein distance to measure closeness to i.i.d., and another based on examining average k-body marginals. Their properties are explored and hierarchical relations with the existing Mazzola et al. definition are proven via explicit counterexamples.
AI.result: A strict hierarchy is established: Mazzola et al.'s notion is the strictest, the Wasserstein-distance-based notion is intermediate, and the k-body marginal notion is the loosest. Strict separation is demonstrated through explicit examples.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a clearer taxonomy of "almost i.i.d." quantum states, offering physically motivated alternatives and clarifying their relative strengths.

title: Extensive long-range magic in non-Abelian topological orders
summary: We show that the low-energy states of non-Abelian topological orders possess extensive magic which is long-ranged, and cannot be eliminated by a constant-depth local unitary circuit. This refines conventional notions of complexity beyond the linear circuit depth which is required to prepare any topological phase, and provides a new resource-theoretic characterization of topological orders. A central technical result is a no-go theorem establishing that stabilizer states--even up to constant-depth local unitarie--cannot approximate low-energy states of non-Abelian string-net models which satisfy the entanglement bootstrap axioms. Moreover, we show that stabilizer-realizable Abelian string-net phases have mutual braiding phases quantized by the on-site qudit dimension, and that any violation of this condition necessarily implies extensive long-range magic. Extending to higher spatial dimensions, we argue that any state obeying an entanglement area law and hosting excitations with nontrivial fusion spaces must exhibit extensive long-range magic. This applies, in particular, to ground-states and low-energy states of higher-dimensional quantum double models.

AI.tldr: Low-energy states of non-Abelian topological orders possess extensive long-range magic that cannot be eliminated by constant-depth local unitary circuits, providing a new resource-theoretic characterization of topological orders.
AI.motivation: To refine conventional notions of complexity in topological phases beyond linear circuit depth, and to establish a resource-theoretic characterization distinguishing Abelian from non-Abelian topological orders based on quantum magic.
AI.method: The paper proves a no-go theorem that stabilizer states (even up to constant-depth local unitaries) cannot approximate low-energy states of non-Abelian string-net models satisfying entanglement bootstrap axioms. It analyzes mutual braiding phases quantized by on-site qudit dimension in stabilizer-realizable Abelian string-net phases, and extends the argument to higher dimensions using entanglement area laws and nontrivial fusion spaces.
AI.result: Non-Abelian topological orders exhibit extensive long-range magic; stabilizer-realizable Abelian phases have braiding phases quantized by qudit dimension; any state with entanglement area law and nontrivial fusion excitations must have extensive long-range magic, including higher-dimensional quantum double models.
AI.conclusion: Extensive long-range magic is a fundamental feature distinguishing non-Abelian topological orders from Abelian ones, serving as a new computational complexity resource that is robust against constant-depth circuits.

title: Universal quantum resource distillation via composite generalised quantum Stein's lemma
summary: The performance of quantum resource manipulation protocols, including key examples such as distillation of quantum entanglement, is measured in terms of the rate at which desired target states can be produced from a given noisy state. However, to achieve optimal rates, known protocols require precise tailoring to the quantum state in question, demanding a perfect knowledge of the input and allowing no errors in its preparation. Here we show that distillation of quantum resources in the framework of resource non-generating operations can be performed universally: optimal rates of distillation can be achieved with no knowledge of the input state whatsoever, certifying the robustness of quantum resource distillation. The findings apply in particular to the purification of quantum entanglement under non-entangling maps, where the optimal rates are governed by the regularised relative entropy of entanglement. Our result relies on an extension of the generalised quantum Stein's lemma in quantum hypothesis testing to a composite setting where the null hypothesis is no longer a fixed quantum state, but is rather composed of i.i.d. copies of an unknown state. The solution of this asymptotic problem is made possible through new developments in one-shot quantum information and a refinement of the blurring technique from [Lami, arXiv:2408.06410].

AI.tldr: This paper shows that quantum resource distillation can be performed universally without knowledge of the input state, achieving optimal rates via resource non-generating operations. This is enabled by extending the generalized quantum Stein's lemma to a composite hypothesis setting and applying new one-shot quantum information techniques and a refined blurring method.
AI.motivation: Quantum resource distillation protocols (e.g., entanglement distillation) require precise tailoring to the specific input state, demanding perfect knowledge and error-free preparation. The paper aims to determine whether such protocols can be made universal—achieving optimal rates without any knowledge of the input state.
AI.method: The work extends the generalized quantum Stein's lemma in quantum hypothesis testing to a composite setting where the null hypothesis consists of i.i.d. copies of an unknown state rather than a fixed state. This is solved via new developments in one-shot quantum information theory and a refinement of the blurring technique from Lami (arXiv:2408.06410).
AI.result: Quantum resource distillation can be performed universally under resource non-generating operations: optimal distillation rates are achievable with no knowledge of the input state. For entanglement distillation under non-entangling maps, optimal rates are governed by the regularised relative entropy of entanglement.
AI.conclusion: The findings certify the robustness of quantum resource distillation, showing that optimal rates do not require state-specific tailoring, which has important implications for practical quantum information processing.

title: Translation symmetry-enforced long-range entanglement in mixed states
summary: We show by a counting argument that even though translation symmetry admits symmetric short-range entangled (SRE) eigenstates, there are not enough such SRE eigenstates to span the zero momentum sector. This means that the fixed point strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking state of translation symmetry is long-range entangled: it cannot be written as a mixture of SRE states. This is a subtle form of long-range entanglement in mixed states that cannot be detected by long-range connected correlation functions.

AI.tldr: Using a counting argument, the paper shows that translation symmetry's zero momentum sector cannot be fully spanned by symmetric short-range entangled (SRE) eigenstates, revealing that the strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking state of translation symmetry is long-range entangled in a subtle way not detectable by standard correlation functions.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the fixed point strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking state of translation symmetry exhibits a subtle form of long-range entanglement in mixed states that cannot be detected by long-range connected correlation functions.
AI.method: A counting argument that shows translation symmetry admits symmetric SRE eigenstates, but there are insufficient such states to span the zero momentum sector.
AI.result: The fixed point strong-to-weak SSB state of translation symmetry is long-range entangled and cannot be expressed as a mixture of SRE states.
AI.conclusion: There exists a subtle form of long-range entanglement in mixed states that evades detection by long-range connected correlation functions.

title: Mixed-State Long-Range Entanglement from Dimensional Constraints
summary: We present a new mechanism for long-range entanglement (LRE) in strongly symmetric many-body mixed states that does not rely on symmetry anomalies or long-range correlations. Our primary example is the maximally mixed state in the translation-invariant subspace on a one-dimensional ring. This state is LRE because translationally symmetric short-range entangled states span a subspace whose dimension grows only polynomially with system size, whereas the full translation-invariant subspace grows exponentially. We further discuss certain unconventional properties of this state, including logarithmically growing conditional mutual information, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry-breaking, and Rényi-index-dependent operator-space entanglement. We also construct a geometrically non-local Lindbladian to stabilize this state as the steady state. Our results identify dimensional mismatch as a novel route to LRE that is intrinsic to many-body mixed states.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies dimensional mismatch as a novel mechanism for long-range entanglement (LRE) in strongly symmetric mixed states, exemplified by the maximally mixed state in the translation-invariant subspace on a 1D ring, which exhibits LRE due to the exponential growth of the subspace versus polynomial growth of symmetric short-range entangled states.
AI.motivation: To uncover a fundamentally new mechanism for long-range entanglement in mixed states that does not rely on symmetry anomalies or long-range correlations, which are the traditional sources of LRE.
AI.method: The authors analyze the maximally mixed state in the translation-invariant subspace on a one-dimensional ring, comparing the dimension of the full translation-invariant subspace (exponential) to that of translationally symmetric short-range entangled states (polynomial). They further characterize this state using conditional mutual information, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking, and Rényi-index-dependent operator-space entanglement, and construct a geometrically non-local Lindbladian that stabilizes it.
AI.result: The translation-invariant maximally mixed state is long-range entangled due to dimensional mismatch. It shows logarithmically growing conditional mutual information, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking, and Rényi-index-dependent operator-space entanglement. A non-local Lindbladian can stabilize this state as a steady state.
AI.conclusion: Dimensional mismatch is identified as a novel route to long-range entanglement intrinsic to many-body mixed states, distinct from previously known mechanisms.
